title: Book I, Aphorisms XXXVIII–LXVIII
author: Francis Bacon
source: *Novum Organum*, Book I, Aphorisms XXXVIII–LXVIII, in the English translation edited by Joseph Devey (New York: P. F. Collier & Son, 1902), 19–43. Bacon published the *Novum Organum* in Latin in 1620.
summary: The four idols that beset the human mind: the idols of the tribe, rooted in human nature itself; of the den, in each man's character and education; of the market, in the words men use; and of the theatre, in the received systems of philosophy, which Bacon divides into the sophistical, the empirical and the superstitious.
